title_en: Ding'an Chengdong Building Decoration Engineering Company v. People's Government of Ding'an County, Hainan Province, and Agricultural Bank of China, Ding'an Sub-branch (Third Party) — Recovery of State-owned Land Use Rights and Revocation of Land Certificate
ruling_gist_en: Where an administrative agency makes an adverse administrative decision against a party without hearing that party's statements and defenses, thereby violating the principle of due process, such action falls under the circumstance of 'violating legal procedures' as provided in subparagraph 3 of paragraph (2) of Article 54 of the Administrative Procedure Law. Where an administrative agency lawfully withdraws state-owned land use rights in accordance with subparagraphs (1) and (2) of paragraph 1 of Article 58 of the Land Administration Law, the compensation to be paid to the land use rights holder shall be based on the market appraised value at the time the decision to withdraw the land use rights was made. If the delay in paying compensation is caused by an illegal administrative compensation decision, the people's court may, based on the party's actual losses and other circumstances, order the administrative agency to bear the loss of bank interest for the same period during the delayed payment of compensation.

full_text_en:
Ding'an Chengdong Building Decoration Engineering Company v. People's Government of Ding'an County, Hainan Province, and Third Party Agricultural Bank of China Ding'an Sub-branch — dispute over recovery of state-owned land use rights and revocation of land certificate

【Ruling Summary】

Where an administrative organ makes an adverse administrative act against a party without hearing that party's statements and defense, violating the principle of due process, such act falls within the circumstance of "violating statutory procedures" under Article 54(2)(3) of the Administrative Procedure Law. Where an administrative organ recovers state-owned land use rights in accordance with law pursuant to Article 58(1)(1) and (2) of the Land Administration Law, the land use right holder shall be compensated based on the market appraised value at the time of the decision to recover the land use rights. Where the delay in payment of compensation is caused by an illegal administrative compensation decision, the people's court may, based on the actual losses of the party and other circumstances, order the administrative organ to bear the interest on bank deposits at the same rate for the period of delayed payment of compensation.

Supreme People's Court Administrative Judgment

(2012) Xing Ti Zi No. 26

Applicant for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Ding'an Chengdong Building Decoration Engineering Company. Address: First Floor, Keze Building, Dazhong Middle Road, Dingcheng Town, Ding'an County, Hainan Province.

Legal Representative: Mo Kerui, Manager.

Agent Ad Litem: Wu Changping, Lawyer, Hainan Pengda Law Firm.

Agent Ad Litem: Mo Keze, Retired Cadre, Ding'an County Administration for Industry and Commerce.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): People's Government of Ding'an County, Hainan Province. Address: Xing'an Avenue, Dingcheng Town, Ding'an County.

Legal Representative: Fu Lidong, County Head.

Agent Ad Litem: Zhou Yijie, Lawyer, Hainan Oriental Guoxin Law Firm.

Agent Ad Litem: Zeng Ping, Civil Servant, Ding'an County Bureau of Land and Environmental Resources.

Third Party at First Instance: Agricultural Bank of China Ding'an Sub-branch.

Person in Charge: He Rigao, Branch Manager.

Agent Ad Litem: He Zhuang, Lawyer, Hainan Jinyu Law Firm.

Agent Ad Litem: Zhong Chong, Legal Counsel of the Branch.

The applicant for retrial, Ding'an Chengdong Building Decoration Engineering Company (hereinafter referred to as Chengdong Company), appealed against the administrative judgment (2008) Qiong Xing Zhong Zi No. 159 rendered by the Hainan High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as Hainan High Court) in the case concerning the recovery of state-owned land use rights and revocation of land certificate against the respondent, the People's Government of Ding'an County (hereinafter referred to as the County Government), and the third party at first instance, Agricultural Bank of China Ding'an Sub-branch (hereinafter referred to as Ding'an Sub-branch), and applied to this court for retrial. Upon review, this court rendered the administrative ruling (2011) Xing Jian Zi No. 91, deciding to bring the case up for retrial, and legally formed a collegial panel. The case was heard in open court on August 30, 2013, in the Third Courtroom of the Hainan High People's Court. Agent ad litem of the applicant for retrial, Wu Changping and Mo Keze; agent ad litem of the respondent, Zhou Yijie and Zeng Ping; and agent ad litem of the third party at first instance, He Zhuang and Zhong Chong, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. During the trial, this court lawfully commissioned Duming United Real Estate Appraisal (Beijing) Co., Ltd. to appraise the value of the land involved, and organized the parties to mediate, but mediation failed. This case is now concluded.

Facts found at first instance:

On September 10, 1994, the Ding'an County Construction Commission (hereinafter referred to as the County Construction Commission) entered into a "Project Contract" with Chengdong Company for the drainage and road paving works on East Cross Street, Renmin North Road, Dingcheng. Subsequently, because the County Construction Commission owed Chengdong Company a project payment of 804,720 yuan, the County Government agreed to allocate 10 mu of land in the Taling Industrial Development Zone as compensation. On October 27, 1995, based on Chengdong Company's submission of a "Request for Readjusting Compensation Land for the Continued Construction Project of East Cross Street, Renmin North Road," the County Government issued Ding Fu Han [1995] No. 117 "Reply on Readjusting Compensation Land for Chengdong Building Decoration Engineering Company," deciding to readjust 10 mu of land near Jianlong Road at a price of 80,000 yuan per mu for Chengdong Company. On December 8 of the same year, the Ding'an County Land Administration Bureau (hereinafter referred to as the County Land Bureau) issued No. 14 "Construction Land Planning Permit" to Chengdong Company. On December 27 of the same year, the County Government issued Ding Fu [1995] No. 299 "Decision on Granting State-Owned Land Use Rights to Ding'an Chengdong Building Decoration Engineering Company," granting 6,706 square meters of land located in the northeast side of Taling Development Zone to Chengdong Company as construction land at a total price of 804,720 yuan. Subsequently, Chengdong Company entered into a "State-Owned Land Use Rights Grant Contract" with the County Land Bureau. On December 28, 1995, Chengdong Company applied for registration and issuance of a certificate for the granted 6,706 square meters of land, but when filling out the application for land registration, it did not specify the land use purpose. During the review process, the County Land Bureau also did not specify the land use purpose in documents such as the "Cadastral Survey Form" and "Land Registration Approval Form." On January 22, 1996, based on Chengdong Company's application and the County Land Bureau's review, and after Chengdong Company paid the land registration fee, the County Government issued to the company Ding'an Guo Yong (96) Zi No. 6 "State-Owned Land Use Certificate" (hereinafter referred to as No. 6 Land Certificate). Thereafter, Chengdong Company operated a cement prefabrication plant on this parcel of land. On November 9, 2001, Chengdong Company used this parcel of land as collateral for a loan from Ding'an Sub-branch and completed mortgage registration at the Ding'an County Construction and Land Environmental Resources Bureau (formerly the County Land Bureau). On January 4, 2004, the County Government published a notice in Hainan Daily on the grounds that Chengdong Company's land was idle, intending to recover the land use rights under No. 6 Land Certificate without compensation, but the County Government did not carry out the uncompensated land recovery. On November 5, 2007, to meet the needs of implementing the urban planning for the Taling Planning New District, the County Government issued Ding Fu [2007] No. 112 "Notice on Compensated Recovery of State-Owned Land Use Rights" (hereinafter referred to as Notice No. 112), deciding to recover the land use rights under No. 6 Land Certificate from Chengdong Company at the original registration cost price of 806,072 yuan, and served it on Chengdong Company on November 8. On December 6 of the same year, the County Construction Bureau (which had been split from the original Ding'an County Construction and Land Environmental Resources Bureau into the Construction Bureau and the Bureau of Land and Environmental Resources) decided to revoke No. 14 "Construction Land Planning Permit," citing that the Hainan Provincial Government had approved on January 27, 2007, the adjustment of the 6,706 square meters of comprehensive public construction land granted to Chengdong Company to administrative office land. On December 7 of the same year, the Ding'an County Bureau of Land and Environmental Resources (hereinafter referred to as the County Land and Resources Bureau) notified Chengdong Company and Ding'an Sub-branch that a hearing would be held on December 11 concerning the compensated recovery of Chengdong Company's state-owned land use rights. Chengdong Company did not attend the hearing. On December 14 of the same year, the County Government, on the grounds that Chengdong Company failed to specify the land use purpose when applying for land registration and certificate issuance, and that the County Land Bureau also failed to specify the land use purpose in documents such as the "Cadastral Survey Form" and "Land Registration Approval Form" during the review process, resulting in erroneous registration and certificate issuance, informed Chengdong Company that it intended to revoke No. 6 Land Certificate. On December 29 of the same year, the County Government issued Ding Fu [2007] No. 150 "Decision on Revoking Ding'an Guo Yong (96) Zi No. 6 'State-Owned Land Use Certificate'" (hereinafter referred to as Decision No. 150), revoking No. 6 Land Certificate. Dissatisfied with this decision, Chengdong Company filed an administrative lawsuit with the former Hainan Hainan Intermediate People's Court (now renamed Hainan First Intermediate People's Court).

Judgment at first instance held: The land in dispute was land that the County Government had compensated to Chengdong Company in 1996 to offset project payments and for which a certificate was issued. According to Article 58 of the Land Administration Law of the People's Republic of China, the County Government may, for the needs of public interest, recover the land use rights in dispute on a compensated basis. However, Notice No. 112 of the County Government decided to recover the land use rights at the original offset price, without considering the factor of land appreciation, making the land recovery action clearly inappropriate. Before issuing Notice No. 112, the County Government did not propose a plan for compensated recovery of state-owned land use rights, and there was a situation where the decision to recover was made before the hearing was held, violating statutory procedures. Given that the land in dispute has now been used by the County Government as administrative office land, revoking Notice No. 112 would cause damage to national interests, so it is not appropriate to order revocation but should confirm its illegality. Article 11 of the Land Registration Rules requires that the land use purpose be stated in the land registration application when applying for land registration. However, the failure to state the land use purpose in the land registration application is not a statutory ground for canceling the land registration. Therefore, the County Government's revocation of No. 6 Land Certificate on the grounds that Chengdong Company failed to fill in the land use purpose when applying for land registration has no legal basis. However, revoking this action has no practical significance, so the illegality of Decision No. 150 should be confirmed. Pursuant to Article 58 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court ruled: 1. Confirming that Notice No. 112 issued by the County Government is illegal. 2. Confirming that Decision No. 150 issued by the County Government is illegal. 3. Ordering the County Government to take remedial measures for the losses incurred by Chengdong Company due to the recovery of state-owned land use rights. The County Government appealed against this judgment.

The Hainan High Court, in its second instance judgment, affirmed the facts found in the first instance judgment, but held that after Chengdong Company obtained the disputed land in January 1996, it did not carry out substantial development of the land, merely operating a simple cement prefabrication plant on it. In January 2004, the County Government, based on the fact that the disputed land had been idle for more than two years, intended to recover the disputed land without compensation. However, in order to protect the lawful rights and interests of Chengdong Company, and considering the actual situation that the land in dispute had been approved by the Hainan Provincial People's Government for use as administrative office land by the County Government, the County Government, pursuant to Article 58(1) of the Land Administration Law, decided to recover the disputed land on a compensated basis. This practice fully protected the lawful rights and interests of Chengdong Company. Therefore, Notice No. 112 issued by the County Government had clear facts and correctly applied the law, and should be upheld. Decision No. 150 issued by the County Government was a refinement of the matters concerning Notice No. 112. Revoking No. 6 Land Certificate did not mean that Chengdong Company's lawful rights and interests could not be protected; it could negotiate with the County Government on the specific plan for compensated land recovery based on Notice No. 112. Pursuant to Article 61(3) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 56(4) and Article 70 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court ruled: 1. Reversing the administrative judgment (2008) Hainan Xing Chu Zi No. 69. 2. Dismissing Chengdong Company's claims.

The applicant for retrial asserts: The findings of the Hainan High Court judgment are contrary to law and fact. First, the land in dispute was undeveloped land in 1996 and was intended for comprehensive industrial, commercial, and residential use. The applicant's land leveling and construction of a cement prefabrication plant were consistent with the planning and constituted substantial development and utilization. Second, the fact that the land was idle for more than two years is untrue. After the land was offset to the applicant, a cement prefabrication plant was built on it and it was never idle. Therefore, the legal provisions on idle land do not apply, nor does the uncompensated recovery apply. This is precisely the reason why, after the respondent published a notice of uncompensated recovery, it later chose compensated recovery on the grounds of public interest. Third, the County Government's construction of its own office building cannot be deemed "public interest," which is contrary to the Land Administration Law of the People's Republic of China. Fourth, "appropriate compensation" should be based on market appraisal. The Hainan High Court's administrative judgment (2008) Qiong Xing Zhong Zi No. 159 erred in the application of law, and the applicant requests its revocation.

The respondent in its defense states: First, the fact that Chengdong Company's land was idle is clear. According to the "State-Owned Land Use Rights Grant Contract" signed between the county land department and Chengdong Company, Chengdong Company was to complete the project construction by December 20, 1997. However, Chengdong Company constructed a cement prefabrication plant that did not conform to the planning, clearly violating Article 29 of the Urban Planning Law of the People's Republic of China, constituting idle land. Second, administrative office land can be defined as "public interest." Referring to Article 8 of the Regulations on the Expropriation and Compensation of Houses on State-Owned Land, public utilities such as municipal and public facilities organized by the government fall within the scope of public interest. Third, the compensation standard for the compensated recovery of land is not inappropriate. The County Government recovered the land use rights in dispute at a price of 806,000 yuan, which was not significantly different from the land price at that time. Chengdong Company did not carry out substantial development and construction on the disputed land for a period of ten years, constituting serious idle land behavior, for which the land could have been recovered without compensation. However, considering social harmony, the County Government chose compensated recovery. The appreciation of idle land should not be borne by the County Government. Chengdong Company's behavior of hoarding land for better prices is not worth promoting.

The third party at first instance in its defense states: First, the land in dispute has undergone mortgage registration procedures, and a certificate of subordinate rights has been obtained. The mortgage right is legally valid, and the priority right to be compensated from the mortgage should be protected by law. Second, Ding'an Sub-branch is a bona fide mortgagee with no fault. If the land use rights in dispute are recovered, it will extinguish the mortgage right, which is obviously unfair and poses a huge risk to transaction security. The County Government should protect the bank's mortgage right based on the principle of fairness. Third, even if the County Government's Notice No. 112 and Decision No. 150 are lawful, pursuant to Article 58 of the Security Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 80 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Security Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 174 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China, Ding'an Sub-branch has the right to be compensated on a priority basis from Chengdong Company's land compensation. Fourth, the County Government's Notice No. 112 and Decision No. 150 are illegal and seriously damage the lawful rights and interests of the mortgagee, and should be revoked according to law. The third party requests support for Chengdong Company's claims and protection of Ding'an Sub-branch's principal claim and mortgage right.

During the trial of this court, except for the following three facts, the parties had no objection to the main facts found in the original trial judgments, and this court confirms them.

1. Chengdong Company objected to the original trial judgment's finding that it "failed to state the land use purpose when applying for land registration and certificate issuance," asserting that the land in dispute was obtained by the County Government as a debt offset for project payments, so the County Government should have handled the registration; the failure to state the land use purpose was not the company's error. The County Government argued that the land in dispute should have been classified as industrial land at the time, but indeed no project was declared, no planning existed, and the land certificate did not specify the purpose; the reason for not specifying the purpose was unknown. Ding'an Sub-branch stated it was unaware of the certificate issuance process.

This court holds that the original trial judgment's finding that "failed to state the land use purpose when applying for land registration and certificate issuance" is merely a statement of fact. The parties have no objection to this fact. The issue of whose fault caused the failure to fill in the information does not belong to the factual determination of this case. Therefore, this court confirms the fact as found in the original trial judgment.

2. Chengdong Company objected to the original trial judgment's finding that it did not attend the hearing, stating that its representative arrived at the venue 10 minutes early but could not enter because the meeting room door was not open; after waiting for about an hour, they left. Chengdong Company also claimed that the hearing record submitted by the County Government at first instance was forged. The County Government argued that it had evidence such as the hearing notice, service acknowledgment, and meeting records, showing that Chengdong Company and Ding'an Sub-branch had been notified in writing to attend the hearing. Ding'an Sub-branch attended, but Chengdong Company did not. Ding'an Sub-branch stated that the person who attended the hearing was indeed its staff member, but expressed no opinion on the authenticity of the hearing record.

This court holds that, based on the hearing notice, service acknowledgment submitted by the County Government at first instance, and the statements of Chengdong Company, it can be established that Chengdong Company and Ding'an Sub-branch were notified in advance to attend the hearing. Based on the hearing meeting record, attendance sheet, and Ding'an Sub-branch's acknowledgment of the attendee's identity, it can be proven that a hearing was held on December 11, 2007, concerning the land recovery. Chengdong Company's assertion that the hearing record was forged is not supported by any evidence, and its defense cannot stand. This court confirms the fact as found in the original trial judgment.

3. The County Government objected to the original trial judgment's finding that Chengdong Company had operated a cement prefabrication plant on the land after obtaining the land certificate, arguing that there was no evidence proving that Chengdong Company had built a cement prefabrication plant on the disputed land. Chengdong Company argued that its business license and photos of the site before demolition could prove the existence of the cement prefabrication plant. Ding'an Sub-branch agreed with Chengdong Company's view.

This court holds that the main business scope of Chengdong Company's 2007 business license included "indoor and outdoor decoration engineering" and "building materials sales," and the site photos showed a building adjacent to the land in dispute and an open space stacked with a large number of prefabricated cement pipes. These items, together with the statements of Chengdong Company and Ding'an Sub-branch, corroborate each other and can establish the fact that a cement prefabrication plant existed on the land in dispute. The County Government's denial of this fact is not supported by sufficient evidence, and this court does not accept it.

During the trial, this court commissioned Duming Appraisal Company to assess the market price of the land in dispute as of November 5, 2007, the date on which the County Government decided to recover the land use rights, on the basis of residential land use. Duming Appraisal Company issued Jing Du Ming Gu F Zi [2013] No. 91292 "Real Estate Appraisal Report," with the appraisal result: the market value of the appraised object as of the appraisal base date was RMB 1,350,000. At the trial, this court conducted an examination of this evidence. Chengdong Company had no objection to the appraisal entity and procedure, but objected to the appraisal result, arguing that using November 5, 2007, as the appraisal base date was inappropriate. The County Government had no objection to the appraisal report. Ding'an Sub-branch indicated that it would express its opinion after consulting relevant persons after the trial. It submitted a written opinion after the trial stating that the appraisal price was significantly lower than the local market price.

This court holds that Duming Appraisal Company and its appraisers possess legal qualifications for land price appraisal, and the appraisal entity is lawful. During the appraisal process, this court organized the appraisal agency and all parties to examine and authenticate the appraisal materials, and conducted a site inspection. The appraisal agency made the appraisal in accordance with the requirements of this court's commission letter and legal procedures. It is not inappropriate to appraise the market price based on the time when the lawful rights and interests of the applicant for retrial were affected by the specific administrative act, i.e., when the County Government decided to recover the land use rights. Ding'an Sub-branch asserts that the appraisal price is significantly lower than the local market price, but does not provide reasons or evidence for the error in the appraisal report. Compared with the market prices of similar land in the same area of Ding'an County at the time of the appraisal, the appraised price of the land in dispute does not appear to be significantly low. The defenses of Chengdong Company and Ding'an Sub-branch cannot stand. The appraisal report is lawful and valid, and this court admits it as evidence.

The main issues in dispute in this case are: First, the legality of the decision to recover land use rights in the challenged Notice No. 112; second, the legality of the administrative compensation decision in the challenged Notice No. 112; and third, the legality of Decision No. 150.

(1) On the legality of the decision to收回 (take back) the land use right in the disputed Document No. 112. Pursuant to Article 58, paragraph 1 of the Land Administration Law of the PRC, the County Government has the statutory authority to收回 the land use right involved with compensation. However, before issuing the disputed Document No. 112, the County Government failed to hear the statements and defenses of the parties, and subsequently notified Chengdong Company and Ding'an Sub-branch to hold a hearing, which violated the basic procedural rule of "hear opinions before making a decision." The State Council's Guofa [2004] No. 10, the "Outline for Comprehensively Promoting Law-based Administration," clearly requires that administrative organs, when implementing administrative management, must follow "due process" and "except for matters involving state secrets, commercially confidential information protected by law, or individual privacy, shall disclose information, pay attention to hearing opinions of citizens, legal persons, and other organizations; and shall strictly follow statutory procedures to protect the rights of administrative counterparts and interested parties to be informed, to participate, and to seek relief in accordance with the law." Before issuing Document No. 112, the County Government did not hear the parties' opinions, which violated the principle of due process, and the decision should have been revoked according to law. However, considering that the County Government's office building has already been completed and put into use, revoking the decision in Document No. 112 to收回 the land use right involved with compensation is no longer practically meaningful and might harm the public interest. In accordance with Article 58 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, the administrative act should be confirmed illegal by judgment.

(2) On the legality of the administrative compensation content in Document No. 112. Pursuant to Article 58, paragraph 2 of the Land Administration Law of the PRC, where it is necessary to use land for public interest purposes and thus收回 the state-owned land use right, appropriate compensation shall be given to the land use right holder. The County Government, in order to construct its office building as required by the overall plan approved by the Provincial Government, needed to use the land involved and收回 the land use right of Chengdong Company, and should have given "appropriate compensation" according to law. The so-called "appropriate compensation" should be fair and reasonable compensation, that is, compensation based on the market appraised value as of the date of the land recovery decision, taking into account the nature, purpose, and location of the land to be recovered. The County Government's compensation based on the original cost of the land lacks legal basis. Chengdong Company argued that because the land recovery decision was illegal and the land use right involved still belonged to it, compensation should be based on the market appraised value at the time of the final judgment. This argument cannot stand. The land recovery decision in this case was procedurally illegal; confirming the illegality of the decision by judgment does not negate its legal effect. Pursuant to Article 28 of the Property Law of the PRC, the land use right involved has already taken effect with the transfer of property rights from the date the land recovery decision became effective. Considering that the "land purpose" column in the registration materials for the land involved is blank, and in light of the local land transaction market conditions, appraising the land involved based on the "residential land" purpose with the longest use period and highest market value is conducive to protecting the legitimate rights and interests of the administrative counterpart. Given that the County Government's act of recovering the land use right was illegal, the compensation price was obviously unfair, and the land involved appreciated significantly after the land recovery decision was made, and the party was unable to repay bank loans in time by transferring the land use right, resulting in loan interest losses, the County Government, while paying the compensation, should also pay the corresponding bank loan interest from the date of the decision to recover the land use right until the actual date of full payment of the compensation.

(3) On the legality of Document No. 150 revoking the certificate. After issuing Document No. 112, the County Government did not require Chengdong Company to submit relevant certification documents to the land management department to apply for cancellation of the land registration. Instead, it issued Document No. 150 to revoke the certificate on the grounds that the "State-owned Land Use Certificate" held by the company did not specify the land purpose as required by Article 11 of the Land Registration Rules, and the land management department also failed to conduct a comprehensive review and fill out the land registration approval form as required by Article 14 of the Land Registration Rules, resulting in erroneous registration and issuance of the certificate. The failure to fill in the land purpose at the outset was not attributable to Chengdong Company and could have been resolved by correction. However, the County Government used this as a reason to revoke the "State-owned Land Use Certificate" lawfully held by Chengdong Company, which constitutes an abuse of administrative power and should be revoked according to law. Considering that the land involved has already been recovered and the office building has been completed and put into use, in accordance with Article 58 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, the administrative act should be confirmed illegal by judgment.

In summary, the land recovery decision in Document No. 112 violated statutory procedures, and the disputed Document No. 150 revoking the certificate constituted an abuse of power; both should be confirmed illegal by judgment. The administrative compensation decision in Document No. 112 involved erroneous application of law, violation of statutory procedures, and was manifestly unfair; it should be corrected according to law. The second-instance judgment dismissing the plaintiff's claims was erroneous and should be revoked according to law. The first-instance judgment confirming the illegality of the administrative compensation decision in Document No. 112 and ordering the County Government to take remedial measures for Chengdong Company's losses was unspecific in content and should be revoked and amended according to law. Chengdong Company's grounds for retrial are partially established and should be supported according to law. The original trial's claim by Ding'an Sub-branch for priority right to be repaid from the mortgaged property is sustainable, and the County Government should protect it according to law when paying compensation. In accordance with Articles 58 and 78 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, the judgment is as follows:

1. Revoke Administrative Judgment (2008) Qiong Xing Zhong Zi No. 159 of the Hainan High People's Court.

2. Affirm the content of Item 1 of Administrative Judgment (2008) Hainan Xing Chu Zi No. 69 of the former Hainan Intermediate People's Court of Hainan Province, confirming the illegality of the part concerning the recovery of state-owned land use right in Ding'an County People's Government's Ding Fu [2007] No. 112 "Notice on the Paid Recovery of State-owned Land Use Rights" dated November 5, 2007; affirm the content of Item 2 of that judgment, confirming the illegality of Ding'an County People's Government's Ding Fu [2007] No. 150 "Decision on Revolving Ding Guo Yong (96) Zi No. 6 'State-owned Land Use Certificate'" dated December 29, 2007.

3. Revoke the content of Item 1 of Administrative Judgment (2008) Hainan Xing Chu Zi No. 69 of the former Hainan Intermediate People's Court of Hainan Province, confirming the illegality of the part concerning "administrative compensation at the cost price of RMB 806,072" to Ding'an Chengdong Building Decoration Engineering Company in Ding'an County People's Government's Ding Fu [2007] No. 112 "Notice on the Paid Recovery of State-owned Land Use Rights" dated November 5, 2007.

4. Revoke Item 3 of Administrative Judgment (2008) Hainan Xing Chu Zi No. 69 of the former Hainan Intermediate People's Court of Hainan Province, ordering Ding'an County People's Government to take remedial measures for the losses from the recovery of Ding'an Chengdong Building Decoration Engineering Company's state-owned land use right; order Ding'an County People's Government to pay Ding'an Chengdong Building Decoration Engineering Company, within 15 days from the date of service of this judgment, a one-time compensation for the recovery of land use right of RMB 1,350,000 and the corresponding bank loan interest (the loan interest shall be calculated from November 5, 2007, until the principal and interest are actually paid in full).

Court acceptance fees for the first and second instances total RMB 100, land appraisal and other fees total RMB 16,776, totaling RMB 16,876, to be borne by Ding'an County People's Government. The above fees have been paid by Ding'an Chengdong Building Decoration Engineering Company, and Ding'an County People's Government shall pay the above amounts together with the compensation and loan interest to Ding'an Chengdong Building Decoration Engineering Company.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Guo Xiujiang

Acting Judge: Geng Baojian

Acting Judge: Shen Xiaoping

March 10, 2014

Clerk: Xu Chao
